To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the beta-subunit is the only 7S storage polypeptide whose mRNA is affected by methionine, that methionine affects beta-subunit mRNA at the transcriptional level, and that methionsine does not promote beta-subunit degradation.
the level of mRNA for the beta-subunit is depressed by exogenous methionine and that the beta-subunit mRNA is not degraded by exogenous methionsine.

the beta-subunit polypeptide of the 7S storage proteins of soybean is not accumulated in soybean cotyledons grown in the presence of exogenous methionine, that this effect is due to the absence of functional mRNA for this polypeptide in methionine-supplied cotyledons, and that methione does not promote degradation or inhibit translation of beta-subunit mRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of storage protein synthesis during the postgermination development of soybean cotyledons.
the regulation of storage protein accumulation in cultured soybean cotyledons.
the effect of exogenous methionine on the accumulation of storage proteins in soybean cotyledons cultured in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
methionine depress the accumulation of the beta polypeptide in soybean cotyledons cultured in the absence of light by inhibiting the synthesis of beta-subunit mRNA.
the beta-subunit is synthesized from methionine-supplied mRNA in soybean cotyledons.
methionine is not an essential component of the 7S beta-subunit mRNA, and that methionsine does not affect stability of the 7s beta-subunit polypeptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
methionine is a specific inhibitor of the accumulation of the beta-polypeptide of 7S protein.
methionine suppresses accumulation of beta-subunit by inhibiting synthesis of functional mRNA for beta-subunit.

the beta-subunit is not synthesized when methionine is present in the cotyledons, and that methionsine inhibits the synthesis of the beta-polypeptide after synthesis of that polypeptide has already started.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the methionine-mediated repression of 7S beta-subunit mRNA is due to a methionine-mediated inhibition of transcription.
the beta-subunit is synthesized in the absence of methionine in cotyledons of soybean seedlings, but that methionine suppresses the synthesis of the beta-polypeptide.
methionine, an amino acid that is essential for plant growth, is also essential for accumulation of a storage protein.
